title: Jonathan Taylor agrees to 2-year extension with Colts: Source
content:
Jonathan Taylor said he wanted to be an Indianapolis “Colt for life.” Now the star running back is one step closer to turning that dream into reality. Taylor agreed to a two-year, $44 million contract extension Thursday with the Colts, according to league sources who spoke anonymously because they were not authorized to speak publicly. The deal is worth up to $47 million and includes $39 million guaranteed. Taylor will now be under contract through the 2028 season.

Taylor was entering the final year of a three-year, $42 million contract extension he inked in October 2023. That lucrative deal came after a public and sometimes bitter back-and-forth between Taylor and his agent, Malki Kawa, and late Colts owner Jim Irsay. Taylor and Irsay even exchanged verbal jabs via social media before Taylor landed a new deal. This time around, the negotiations went a lot smoother, as the 2020 second-round pick participated in training camp and was rewarded with a third contract from the team that drafted him, which is an increasing rarity for running backs.

The new deal puts Taylor at $22 million in terms of average annual salary, second among running backs. He trails only the Atlanta Falcons’ Bijan Robinson ($22.25 million).

“I’d definitely love to be a Colt for life. I think I’ve already expressed that to them throughout the years,” Taylor said during minicamp. “… Hopefully they feel the same (way) because this is a special place. Not every building is like this, and I’ve heard some stories now, especially from guys coming from other places, and it’s not like this elsewhere.”

Taylor, 27, is coming off an impressive 2025 campaign that at one point had him in the league MVP conversation. He appeared in every game and registered 1,585 rushing yards, his most in a season since earning a first-team All-Pro nod in 2021. Additionally, Taylor’s league-leading 20 total touchdowns (18 rushing and two receiving) last year are tied with Hall of Famer Lenny Moore for the most in a single season in Colts history. Taylor is the only Colts player to reach that threshold twice (2021 and 2025).

Taylor’s new deal confirms that the Colts view him as a part of their long-term future, even if the man who brought him to Indianapolis may not be around. Colts general manager Chris Ballard is entering the final year of his contract, and it’s fair to consider that if Indianapolis misses the playoffs for a sixth straight season, Ballard could be relieved of his duties.

Ballard traded up three spots to select Taylor with the No. 41 pick in the second round of the 2020 NFL Draft. The former Wisconsin standout has had some durability issues throughout his pro career, missing at least three games in each of the 2022, 2023 and 2024 seasons. Despite those absences, Taylor has still emerged as one of the league’s premier running backs.

Taylor’s career average of 90.5 rushing yards per game is the most among active players and ranks fifth all-time behind Hall of Famers Jim Brown, Barry Sanders, Terrell Davis and Eric Dickerson, respectively. Taylor, a three-time Pro Bowler, ranks first in Colts history with 69 rushing TDs. His 7,598 rushing yards are second in franchise history only to Hall of Famer Edgerrin James (9,226).
